topics.title: Excrement Spelling & Muslim Baby Names
topics.summary: A caller obsessively spells 'eat' while describing his habit of writing excrement with a dictionary and discussing a new Muslim baby name selected by Louis Farrakhan, followed by neighborhood development concerns and financial contributions to the Brawley defense fund.

topics.title: Blindfold Radio Mishap with Tom Jones
topics.summary: During a radio segment featuring Howard and Robin wearing blindfolds, they attempt to identify mystery guest Tom Jones. The conversation devolves into chaotic arguments about clues, equipment malfunctions, and personal questions regarding his life and relationships, culminating in an unexpected reveal of his identity.

topics.title: Tom Jones Discusses Associates and Music
topics.summary: During an interview, Tom Jones discusses his acquaintances including Murrah, Johnny Carson, and Elvis Presley while preferring spending time with people he works with in Los Angeles over show business figures. He expresses skepticism towards Scientology and shares anecdotes about a brief encounter with Elvis, discussing writing a book.

topics.title: Jones & Elvis Cap Discussion
topics.summary: Howard interviews Tom Jones about his influence on Elvis’ stage costumes, specifically ‘kooky caps.’ The conversation drifts into mocking Italian stereotypes before revisiting Robert Reid's erratic behavior and exploring the idea of Gary’s new publicity person.

topics.title: Stern’s Misogynistic Remarks & Mattress Obsessions
topics.summary: During the broadcast, Howard Stern repeatedly expresses misogynistic views, criticizing callers for their perceived lack of intelligence or attractiveness. He makes crude remarks about women's appearances and hygiene habits, including comparing them to snakes and suggesting they change mattresses frequently due to unwanted smells. The conversation also includes discussions regarding age gaps in relationships.

topics.title: Brenner’s Hollywood Squares Mishap
topics.summary: Howard Brenner recounts his bizarre experience on Hollywood Squares, including being tied in the trunk of a car by an obsessed fan seeking his ex-girlfriend and subsequent interactions with Rick Rosner and questions about Mayor Koch's finances. He describes awkward encounters and ultimately concludes that he was unfairly edited out of the show. 54 words.
